A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3D-PC study. Their text, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original human and DNN experiments on depth order, VPT-basic and VPT-Strategy, including accuracies, error-pattern comparisons and fine-tuning results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds attribution-localization correlations, further attribution examples and a chain-of-thought prompting finding.

M1.justification: The proposed Co3D/Gaussian-Splatting/Unity generation pipeline and benchmark construction remain unchanged. Chain-of-thought prompting is an added evaluation condition for existing VLMs, rather than a revision to the proposed benchmark method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three tasks using the same Co3D-derived scene coverage and human participant groups. The new prompting and attribution analyses concern retained tasks and data, rather than new domains or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Appendix A.7 adds a chain-of-thought prompting comparison for VLMs alongside the existing answer-only prompting evaluation. No new model family is established: AlexNet gains a Table 1 row, but v1 already explicitly described it as evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds worked chain-of-thought prompt examples and a quantitative attribution-overlap evaluation using Dice similarity. Existing dataset splits, training budgets, hyperparameters and human testing procedures remain unchanged; the shared 94-image test set was already documented in v1.

E4.justification: v1 offered qualitative ViT attribution examples in Figure 6. v2 substantially extends the failure analysis by quantifying target-object localization across the DNNs tested on VPT-Strategy and relating it to accuracy (Figure 10). It also adds a chain-of-thought diagnostic and further attribution case studies (Figure 11).

E5.justification: Human SEM reporting, label-permutation/randomization testing and averaging the best three VLM runs across tested temperatures are retained. Figure 3's added significance brackets visualize findings already reported in v1. No new seed, repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation practice is documented.

E6.justification: Primary benchmark results remain unchanged, including human depth-order/VPT-basic accuracies of 74.73%/86.82% and VPT-Strategy accuracies of 87% for humans versus 66% for the best DNN. Supplementary additions include chance-level VPT performance with chain-of-thought prompting and localization correlations of 0.30, 0.47 and 0.49 with ImageNet, depth-order and VPT-basic accuracy respectively (Figure 10; all p < 0.001).

T1.justification: Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and no substantive mathematical definition or derivation changes. Dice similarity is introduced as an empirical evaluation metric without new formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The central claims about strong depth-order performance, weak VPT and poor generalization remain. v2's contribution list adds the more specific claim that DNNs overuse object size and location instead of estimating line-of-sight, and explicitly includes Gaussian Splatting models among released resources.

C2.justification: v2 strengthens the existing shortcut interpretation into a more specific size/location-based account. Its expanded limitations acknowledge that the depth cues used by humans and DNNs were not isolated and that precisely how DNNs use object features for VPT remains unresolved. The earlier basic-VPT scope limitation is retained.

D1.justification: Resource documentation changes substantially: v2 advertises code, data and Gaussian Splatting models through Hugging Face instead of GitHub and supplies chain-of-thought templates. Conversely, it removes the dataset datasheet and consent screenshot, losing explicit label encoding, Co3D licensing and maintenance/versioning information. Core generation and training details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Dice (1945) and ReCapture (Zhang et al., 2024), and expands related work to discuss explicitly trained 3D systems alongside emergent 3D capabilities. The overall research positioning is retained; the additional AlexNet bibliography entry represents an already cited work.

P1.justification: The supplementary document is substantially restructured through removal of the author checklist and multi-part dataset datasheet and insertion of a chain-of-thought section. Related-work, VPT-Strategy and limitations passages are expanded or rewritten, although the main section sequence and much of its prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 7, 10 and 11, replaces illustrative scenes in Figure 1, adds significance annotations to Figure 3 and revises labels/markers in the former Figure A.3, now Figure 9. It removes the consent screenshot, adds an AlexNet inventory row and adopts the ICLR layout. Core benchmark plots in Figures 4–6 are retained.

improvement.justification: The broader attribution analysis, chain-of-thought check and more specific limitations modestly strengthen the paper's diagnostic evidence and transparency about unresolved mechanisms. These gains are tempered by lost dataset documentation and stronger memorization claims than localization correlations alone establish. The central benchmark evidence remains unchanged, so the improvement is limited rather than transformative.
